fixtures.name: Finite verification promoted to RH
fixtures.invalid_inference: All zeros checked up to height H lie on the line, therefore every nontrivial zero lies on the line.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The universal height quantifier was replaced by one bounded interval.
fixtures.witness: A hypothetical off-line zero with ordinate greater than H is compatible with the finite certificate.
fixtures.remediation: Report only the exact certified interval or supply a global theorem excluding zeros above H.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not discredit rigorous finite-height verification or its finite consequences.

fixtures.name: Density or almost-all result promoted to universality
fixtures.invalid_inference: N0(T)/N(T) tends to one, or a positive proportion lies on the line, therefore RH holds.
fixtures.missing_obligation: A density-zero exceptional set may still be infinite and contain off-line zeros.
fixtures.witness: The set of squares has density zero in the integers but is infinite; density alone does not imply emptiness.
fixtures.remediation: Add a theorem excluding every exceptional zero, not merely bounding their density.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not weaken the valid proportion or density theorem.

fixtures.name: Quartet symmetry used as a location theorem
fixtures.invalid_inference: Conjugation and rho↦1-rho symmetry force each zero to have real part one-half.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Invariance of a set under reflections does not imply every point is fixed by the reflections.
fixtures.witness: Any beta+i gamma with beta≠1/2 generates a symmetry-compatible quartet.
fixtures.remediation: Supply an independent coercive mechanism excluding off-line quartets.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not challenge the functional equation or zero symmetries.

fixtures.name: Euler product continued termwise into the critical strip
fixtures.invalid_inference: The Euler product has no zero factors, so zeta has no zeros throughout the continued domain.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The Euler product is absolutely convergent only for Re(s)>1 and cannot be continued termwise as a nonvanishing product.
fixtures.witness: A representation may define an analytic function on one domain while its termwise product diverges elsewhere.
fixtures.remediation: Use a representation valid on the target domain and prove its convergence and nonvanishing there.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not affect the valid zero-free conclusion for Re(s)>1.

fixtures.name: Conditionally convergent zero sum rearranged
fixtures.invalid_inference: A formally rearranged sum over zeros has a desired sign, so all zeros lie on the line.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The sum is not absolutely convergent and no symmetric truncation or regularization was fixed.
fixtures.witness: Conditionally convergent series can change value under rearrangement.
fixtures.remediation: Declare the limiting order or regularization and prove convergence before using sign or equality.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not exclude correctly regularized Hadamard-product or explicit-formula arguments.

fixtures.name: Global logarithm of zeta assumed
fixtures.invalid_inference: Differentiate or integrate a single-valued Log zeta across the strip.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Zeros and the pole obstruct a global analytic logarithm.
fixtures.witness: The logarithm of a holomorphic function exists analytically only on a suitable zero-free simply connected domain.
fixtures.remediation: Restrict to a declared zero-free simply connected domain or work with zeta'/zeta and account for residues.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not prohibit local analytic logarithms.

fixtures.name: Contour moved without residue ledger
fixtures.invalid_inference: Shift a contour across the pole or zeros and keep the same integral identity.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Crossed singularities contribute residues and horizontal/limiting contours require bounds.
fixtures.witness: The residue theorem changes the integral by 2pi i times the sum of crossed residues.
fixtures.remediation: List every crossed pole/zero, its order and residue, and prove all boundary limits.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not rule out a correctly justified contour shift.

fixtures.name: Sum, integral, derivative, or limit interchanged formally
fixtures.invalid_inference: Exchange analytic operations in an infinite zeta or zero expansion without a convergence theorem.
fixtures.missing_obligation: No domination, uniform convergence, absolute convergence, or closed-operator theorem is supplied.
fixtures.witness: Pointwise convergence alone does not justify differentiation or integration term by term.
fixtures.remediation: Name the exact convergence theorem and verify its hypotheses on the full domain.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not rule out exchanges supported by uniform or dominated convergence.

fixtures.name: Positivity checked on sampled test functions
fixtures.invalid_inference: A Weil-type quadratic form is positive for a large finite library, therefore RH.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The criterion quantifies over an exact infinite test class or its proven dense core.
fixtures.witness: A continuous form can be negative in an unsampled direction unless density and continuity control are established.
fixtures.remediation: Fix the test space, prove density of the checked core, and prove continuity/closure of the form.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not diminish sampled positivity as regression evidence.

fixtures.name: Symmetric operator identified as self-adjoint
fixtures.invalid_inference: A formally Hermitian differential expression has real spectrum, hence gives RH.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Operator symmetry on a core does not determine the self-adjoint domain or deficiency indices.
fixtures.witness: The derivative operator on an interval has different symmetric and self-adjoint domain choices.
fixtures.remediation: Specify the Hilbert space and domain and prove self-adjointness or essential self-adjointness.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not exclude a valid Hilbert–Pólya construction.

fixtures.name: Partial spectral match promoted to exact correspondence
fixtures.invalid_inference: Several eigenvalues or spacing statistics match zero ordinates, so the operator proves RH.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Missing zeros, extraneous spectrum, multiplicities, and continuous spectrum are uncontrolled.
fixtures.witness: Two sequences can agree for arbitrarily many initial terms and then diverge.
fixtures.remediation: Prove a complete multiplicity-preserving spectral equality and exclude all extraneous spectrum.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not deny the heuristic value of spectral statistics.

fixtures.name: Finite Li positivity promoted to the Li criterion
fixtures.invalid_inference: lambda_1 through lambda_N are positive, therefore every lambda_n is nonnegative.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The criterion has a universal quantifier over all positive integers.
fixtures.witness: A sequence may be positive for any prescribed finite prefix and negative later.
fixtures.remediation: Supply a uniform proof for arbitrary n or a theorem controlling the entire tail.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not invalidate certified finite Li-coefficient calculations.

fixtures.name: Near-looking prime error substituted for the exact equivalent
fixtures.invalid_inference: An error term resembling sqrt(x) times logarithms is treated as the Bombieri/Titchmarsh RH equivalent.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The exponent, logarithmic power, counting function, uniformity, and converse direction are not preserved.
fixtures.witness: Bounds for pi, theta, psi, or smoothed functions transfer only through explicit partial summation and prime-power corrections.
fixtures.remediation: State the exact function and bound, prove conversion terms, and reconstruct both implications.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not rule out stronger correctly normalized prime-error estimates.

fixtures.name: One epsilon used for the Mertens criterion
fixtures.invalid_inference: M(x)=O(x^(1/2+epsilon_0)) for one fixed epsilon_0>0, therefore RH.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The equivalence quantifies over every epsilon>0.
fixtures.witness: A single exponent 1/2+epsilon_0 is compatible with zeros whose real part lies between 1/2 and 1/2+epsilon_0.
fixtures.remediation: Prove the family for arbitrary epsilon with explicit dependence of the constant.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not weaken a valid fixed-epsilon estimate.

fixtures.name: GRH or finite-field analogue substituted for classical RH
fixtures.invalid_inference: Evidence or a theorem for another L-function family or zeta function proves the classical zeta statement.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The analytic object, Euler factors, gamma factors, and zero multiset differ.
fixtures.witness: A theorem for a family does not specialize unless the classical zeta function is explicitly included with all conventions matched.
fixtures.remediation: Provide a valid specialization or comparison theorem to the locked classical zeta function.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not diminish genuine analogies or stronger theorems that explicitly include classical zeta.

fixtures.name: Simplicity assumed at a decisive step
fixtures.invalid_inference: Every zero is simple, so a sign-change or derivative argument counts all zeros and proves RH.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Global simplicity is a separate unproved conjecture; sign changes can miss even multiplicity.
fixtures.witness: A real entire function may touch zero with even multiplicity without changing sign.
fixtures.remediation: Make the argument multiplicity-safe or prove simplicity under the exact required scope.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not affect the certified simplicity statement below 3·10^12.

fixtures.name: Zero-free region asymptotically squeezed to the critical line
fixtures.invalid_inference: A zero-free region near Re(s)=1 improves with height, so all zeros must approach Re(s)=1/2.
fixtures.missing_obligation: The region excludes only points near one and supplies no uniform exclusion of every beta>1/2.
fixtures.witness: The boundary 1-c/(log t)^(2/3)(loglog t)^(1/3) tends to one, not one-half.
fixtures.remediation: Prove a zero-free half-strip Re(s)>1/2 or another theorem excluding every off-line beta.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not weaken the prime-distribution consequences of zero-free regions.

fixtures.name: Rouché theorem invoked without boundary control
fixtures.invalid_inference: Two functions look close numerically inside a contour, so they have the same zeros.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Rouché requires a strict inequality on every boundary point and a zero-free boundary.
fixtures.witness: A single uncontrolled boundary point can invalidate the zero count.
fixtures.remediation: Certify |f-g|<|f| or the chosen alternative uniformly on the entire contour.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not rule out interval-certified Rouché arguments.

fixtures.name: Floating-point off-line root promoted to a counterexample
fixtures.invalid_inference: A numerical solver returns beta+i gamma with beta≠1/2 and small |zeta|, so RH is false.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Small residual is not exact vanishing; conditioning, cancellation, and solver error are uncontrolled.
fixtures.witness: Analytic functions can take arbitrarily small nonzero values near a point without vanishing there.
fixtures.remediation: Give an interval enclosure, argument-principle zero count, and certified separation from the critical line.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not rule out a rigorously certified off-line zero as a terminal refutation.

fixtures.name: Zero or pole inferred from one factor of the completion
fixtures.invalid_inference: A zero or pole of Gamma, s(s-1), or zeta alone determines the order of xi without local accounting.
fixtures.missing_obligation: Zeros and poles of the remaining factors may cancel or change the local order.
fixtures.witness: At negative even integers, the zeta zero and Gamma pole must be combined locally.
fixtures.remediation: Compute the local order of every factor in the complete product.
fixtures.does_not_rule_out: This does not challenge the correctly derived trivial-zero taxonomy.
